facts.text: Decision variables for collision-mitigation tuning are detection confidence thresholds, warning and brake zone dimensions per speed, track-confirmation filters (N-of-M frames), persistence and debounce times, time-to-collision triggers and filter constants.
facts.quote: The decision variables are detection confidence thresholds, warning and brake zone dimensions per speed, track-confirmation filters (N-of-M frames), persistence and debounce times, time-to-collision triggers and filter constants.

facts.text: Outcomes for collision-mitigation tuning are missed or late interventions, false warnings per hour, unnecessary brake events per hour, intervention timing (early or late braking), and productivity loss measured as time stopped.
facts.quote: The outcomes are (i) missed or late interventions, (ii) false warnings per hour, (iii) unnecessary brake events per hour, (iv) intervention timing (early or late braking) and (v) productivity loss (time stopped).

facts.text: Collision-mitigation tuning should not begin by combining all outcomes into one weighted scalar cost, because the safety objectives have different meanings.
facts.quote: Do not begin by adding all outcomes into one weighted scalar cost; the safety objectives have different meanings.

facts.text: Published guidance supports a hierarchy for collision-mitigation optimisation; the passage labels this position as expert opinion supported by the optimisation literature.
facts.quote: The published guidance supports a hierarchy. **Expert opinion**, supported by the optimisation literature [25, 45, 46].

facts.text: Collision-mitigation tuning should first impose hard safety constraints on minimum stopping margin, maximum permitted miss probability, maximum intervention latency and required coverage of particular hazardous scenarios.
facts.quote: Impose hard safety constraints first: minimum stopping margin, maximum permitted miss probability (for example zero misses in critical scenarios), maximum intervention latency, required coverage of particular hazardous scenarios.

facts.text: Zero misses in critical scenarios is an example of a maximum permitted miss-probability constraint for collision-mitigation tuning.
facts.quote: maximum permitted miss probability (for example zero misses in critical scenarios)

facts.text: Within the region satisfying the hard safety constraints, collision-mitigation tuning should optimise false warning and intervention rates, comfort, productivity loss and early or late braking.
facts.quote: Within the feasible region, optimise false warning and intervention rates, comfort, productivity loss and early or late braking.

facts.text: Collision-mitigation tuning should preserve a Pareto frontier so engineering and safety authorities can see exactly what is traded.
facts.quote: Preserve a Pareto frontier so engineering and safety authorities can see exactly what is traded.
